title: Smooth convex-concave saddle-point problems: exact scalar values on the full space

assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.
assumptions.description: The function $f:\mathbb R^{d_x+d_y}\to\mathbb R$ is continuously differentiable, convex on $x$, and concave on $y$, with globally $\beta$-Lipschitz joint gradient. Bilinearity and a separate gradient-norm bound are not assumed.

assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.
assumptions.description: The ball radius $R_x,R_y>0$ and dimension are public. Compact convex output domains ensure a saddle point and finite global gap.

model.parameter_domain_description: $R_x$: positive real; $R_y$: positive real; $\beta$: positive real; $d_x$: positive integer; $d_y$: positive integer; $\varepsilon$: positive real. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table; additional accuracy and dimension conditions appear in each regime.
description_paragraphs: The function $f:\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_y}\to\mathbb{R}$ is continuously differentiable, convex on $x$, and concave on $y$, with globally $\beta$-Lipschitz joint gradient. Bilinearity and a separate gradient-norm bound are not assumed.
The ball radius $R_x,R_y>0$ and dimension are public. Compact convex output domains ensure a saddle point and finite global gap.

oracle.operation: query arbitrary full-space z, receive scalar f(z) exactly
oracle.geometry: known balls and exact projection; internal computations not charged as values
oracle.precision: exact noiseless values; finite-precision or stochastic observations require another spec

operations.order_convention: This operation is charged according to its explicit input and output, not renamed according to a scalar function's derivative order.

feedback_quality.description: Exact responses from the same hidden object fixed before interaction

operations.coupling: The exact response map is fixed before interaction; repeated calls are charged separately.

auxiliary_interfaces: Projection uses the stated interface. Internal models defined by already returned data may be solved exactly.
oracle.query_domain_description: Each operation's query_signature is the authoritative query domain. Permissions for queries outside the ball or restrictions to feasible queries are enforced separately for each interface.
description_paragraphs: Public inputs comprise the block dimensions $d_x,d_y$ and parameters $R_x$, $R_y$, $\beta$, and $\varepsilon$, together with the stated initial point and feasible-set information. Analytic descriptions of hidden functions, operators, and matrices are not supplied.

Scalar values are exact and noiseless. Queries may lie outside the output ball, with arbitrarily small separations and no charge for real precision. Projection onto the known ball is internal computation.

output.postprocessing: arbitrary measurable transcript-based output unless algorithm restriction expressly states otherwise
output.allowed_postprocessing: The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.
output.certificate_requirement: No additional computable certificate is required beyond any graph element explicitly listed in the output.
description_paragraphs: The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.

metric.normalization: The exact formula governs; norms, squares, maxima, and expectations are not interchanged.
metric.finiteness_conditions: Use the compact-domain, solution-existence, and smoothness assumptions in the model and the stated metric definition.

resource.budget: fixed worst-case cap on every transcript
resource.auxiliary: projection/internal model solves separately retained, never counted as hidden oracle

components.description: The number of exact scalar-value calls.

resource.scalarization: Keep joint budgets when cost weights are unspecified. Project only onto an explicitly designated primary query coordinate.
resource.setup_cost: All charged initialization queries are included in the total budget.
resource.amortization_scope: One instance and one accuracy target.
resource.precision_model: Exact real information; internal arithmetic, storage, and bit costs are excluded from the query count.
description_paragraphs: Each scalar evaluation costs one $N_{\rm value}$ call. Several evaluation points in an iteration cannot be bundled into one call.
Use a fixed worst-case budget: calls never exceed the prespecified $N$ on any instance or random execution path. Earlier stopping within the budget is permitted.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.

algorithms.adaptivity: Arbitrary measurable sequentially adaptive queries and output
algorithms.internal_computation: Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.
algorithms.parallelism: Sequential query count; a parallel batch is not counted as one query.
description_paragraphs: Arbitrary measurable sequential adaptive randomized algorithms are allowed. The private seed is independent of the hidden instance. Queries, stopping, and output may use the full history, without additional span, zero-respecting, communication, or memory restrictions.

guarantees.complete_expression: \exists\mathcal A\ \forall I:\quad \Pr(\max_{v\in R_yB_2^{d_y}}f(\widehat x,v)-\min_{u\in R_xB_2^{d_x}}f(u,\widehat y)\le\varepsilon)\ge2/3
aggregation_order: First fix the public input and the algorithm.
Apply the stated probability or expectation to the complete error expression.
randomness_sources: Private random seed of the algorithm
guarantees.time_uniformity: A fixed accuracy requirement, not an anytime guarantee.
description_paragraphs: A single algorithm is chosen from the public input and must satisfy the guarantee for every fixed admissible instance.
Probability is over private algorithmic randomness only. The unknown instance is fixed before interaction.

budget.precision_model: Exact real information; internal arithmetic, storage, and bit costs are excluded from the query count.
budget.scalarization: Keep joint budgets when cost weights are unspecified. Project only onto an explicitly designated primary query coordinate.

objects.definition: Unknown real-valued payoff function $f:\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathbb R^{d_y}\to\mathbb R$.
The feasible set is explicitly public. Exact projections and linear algebra use known geometry and reveal no hidden-function information.

domains.definition: The explicit domain of each operation’s query_signature.

Output $(\widehat x,\widehat y)\in R_xB_2^{d_x}\times R_yB_2^{d_y}$. Arbitrary measurable transcript-based postprocessing is permitted, including an unqueried point, an average, or a convex combination, provided the output remains feasible. No additional value or computable accuracy certificate is required.

The function $f:\mathbb R^{d_x+d_y}\to\mathbb R$ is continuously differentiable, convex on $x$, and concave on $y$, with globally $\beta$-Lipschitz joint gradient. Bilinearity and a separate gradient-norm bound are not assumed.

norms.definition: The Euclidean norm and inner product are $\|v\|_2=(\sum_jv_j^2)^{1/2}$ and $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_j u_jv_j$. On the joint space use $\|(x,y)\|_2=(\|x\|_2^2+\|y\|_2^2)^{1/2}$.

quantities.label: Minimum charged resource attaining the stated success guarantee
quantities.analysis_scope: The full documented parameter domain; no upper or lower bound is admitted for this comparison.
quantities.expression_latex: C^\star_{v,\pi}(\varepsilon;\theta)=\inf\{B\ge0:\exists\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_v,\ C_\pi(\mathcal A,I)\le B\ \text{and}\ G_v(\mathcal A,I;\varepsilon)\ \forall I\}
quantities.definition_note: Here v is the selected algorithm view, G_v its complete success guarantee, I an admissible fixed instance, theta the remaining parameters, and C_pi the declared resource projection. C_pi uses the view's fixed-path or expected-work budget convention, including initialization. No change of guarantee or scalarization is implicit.
